spec.name: closed-pipe-convicts
spec.intent: Census @8d0a7283 (design at 8d0a7283; notebook at 8d0a7283 plus the decision note "mav's cell restates its role"); every path is repo-relative on the plan's line. A line number, count or observed behaviour cited here is a measurement at that commit: re-derive it if its path changed since. Add no new test file: a new one must be classified in packages/canon/test/gate-convicts.test.ts, which no unit of this plan owns; extend the test files named in outputs. The command line follows the conventions of any Unix tool, and packages/cli/test/closed-pipe.test.ts holds one of them on the built bin: a reader that closes the pipe early ends the command quietly, with success. Its `--help` and `plan --help` cases pass with the line installing endOnClosedStdout removed from packages/cli/src/cratylus.ts, because commander writes the help in one write that lands before the reader closes; only the `project --verbose` case raises EPIPE (note 'closed-pipe help cases convict nothing'). Make every case convict: the reader closes before the child's first write reaches it (for instance the pipe's read end closed as soon as the child is spawned), so a command that does not end on EPIPE fails each of the three cases. Keep the three cases and their names. Change no source file: the behaviour holds and the proof is what is weak. No changeset (a test alone changes).
accept: with packages/cli and the packages it depends on built, `pnpm exec vitest run test/closed-pipe.test.ts` in packages/cli exits 0

with the line that installs endOnClosedStdout removed from packages/cli/src/cratylus.ts and packages/cli rebuilt, the same run fails all three cases, `--help` and `plan --help` among them (at 8d0a7283 only the project case fails); the line is restored afterwards and `git diff` shows no change under packages/cli/src
